title: Insulation Rebates in Penticton 2026: Up to $5,500 from FortisBC
desc: Penticton runs its own electric utility, and FortisBC rebates cover its customers. 46% of households live in pre-1981 homes. The formula, a worked example and how to claim.
lead: Penticton buys power from the City's own electric utility, not BC Hydro. FortisBC's rebates are the ones that cover Penticton electric customers, and 46% of Penticton households live in homes built before 1981.
cards_heading: What BC Hydro pays for insulation in Penticton
cards_intro: FortisBC lists its insulation rebate for FortisBC gas customers and for FortisBC or municipal electric customers, including Penticton. It uses the same formula as BC Hydro. We checked BC Hydro's page on October 2, 2026 and FortisBC's listing against it. FortisBC also requires that your main heating system can heat at least half your home through the winter to 22°C.

cards.title: Attic
cards.amount: $0.02 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Capped at $900, at least R12 added.

cards.title: Walls and basement
cards.amount: $0.09 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Capped at $1,200 each for wall cavity, sheathing, and basement or crawlspace.

cards.title: Floors and other spots
cards.amount: $0.07 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Capped at $1,000, at least R20 added.

cards.title: Second-upgrade bonus
cards.note: FortisBC adds $300 for a second upgrade, or an EnerGuide improvement bonus of $750 to $2,000.

cards.title: Lower incomes
cards.note: Income-qualified FortisBC customers can get free evaluations and upgrades.

after_cards:
A Penticton 1960s bungalow

A 1,100 square foot attic at R-14 topped to R-50 adds R-36. The formula gives 0.02 x 36 x 1,100 = $792. Adding R-10 to 600 square feet of basement wall pays 0.09 x 10 x 600 = $540. That is $1,332, by our arithmetic on the published formula.
sections: Penticton's electricity comes from the City of Penticton, not BC Hydro. BC Hydro's rebate is only for BC Hydro accounts or a municipal utility inside BC Hydro territory, like New Westminster. FortisBC's listing names Penticton, Summerland, Grand Forks and Nelson Hydro customers, so a Penticton household uses FortisBC for insulation. Call FortisBC's electricity rebate line if your bill shows anything unusual.

The 2021 Census counted 17,360 households in Penticton. Of those, 7,900 (46%) live in homes built before 1981, and 3,440 are owner-occupied detached houses from that era. About 36% of households live in apartments and 37% rent, so a good share of Penticton cannot use a home rebate. Condo owners should look at BC Hydro's Condo and Apartment Rebate Program, but check whether it covers your utility.
A dry, hot summer city too

Penticton's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was -2.5°C and the coldest day was -24.8°C. Summers are hot and dry. Insulation in the attic slows summer heat as well as winter loss, which helps if you run air conditioning or a heat pump in cooling mode.
Rules to check before you book

• FortisBC needs a primary heating system that can heat at least half the home to 22°C.
  • Rebates are calculated on the R-value of new insulation added.
  • If old insulation is removed because of pests or mould, the program assumes a starting R-value for the age of your home.
  • Check FortisBC's listing for the current contractor wording before you sign.

Rebates are paid on the R-value of the new insulation you add, so compare quotes by finished R-value, not by thickness. BC Hydro's page lists batts, loose fill, board and spray foam as eligible types, and FortisBC uses the same formula. Penticton's older bungalows usually need loose fill in the attic and blown-in material for closed walls. A rebate cannot exceed the cost on your invoice, so a small job is paid at what you paid.
FortisBC runs a free home evaluation and upgrade program for income-qualified customers. Some homes may receive free insulation. Ask before paying for any work.
claim_steps: Confirm your electricity is from the City of Penticton or your gas is from FortisBC.
Get quotes that list the R-value added and area for each space.
Apply to FortisBC online. Rebate partners share one form.
If your income may qualify, ask about the free program first.
faq: Do I apply to BC Hydro in Penticton?
No. BC Hydro's rebate needs a BC Hydro account. FortisBC's listing covers Penticton's municipal electric customers.
Is there a bonus for a second upgrade?
FortisBC lists $300 for a second upgrade, or an EnerGuide improvement bonus of $750 to $2,000.
The average January low from 2015 to 2024 was -2.5°C and the coldest day was -24.8°C.
What if I heat with gas?
FortisBC's rebate covers gas customers using the same formula.
No. The home rebate does not cover condos or apartments.
